The main proposal is **adversarial training**: generate deliberately perturbed examples and include them in the training data, so the classifier learns to resist those attacks when classifying new inputs. The survey describes this as among the most effective defenses. (https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.03824)

Other proposed approaches include:
- **Reducing prediction sensitivity:** train models to minimize how much small input perturbations affect their predictions. (https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.03824)
- **Learning more robust features:** train models to rely on less-superficial features that align better with human vision, rather than features vulnerable to subtle changes. (https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.03824)
- **Provable defenses:** seek theoretical guarantees on worst-case model performance under adversarial attack, providing assurance about robustness. (https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.03824)

These are not necessarily complete protections: one passage reports that adversarial training improves robustness for certain perturbation sizes but can remain vulnerable to slightly larger changes. (https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.10513)
